subject: Upfront credits vs monthly invoice — options and next steps
messages:
From: Drew Collins <drew@acme-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Billing cadence and invoicing for hosted API

Hi Ben,

Quick one from procurement as we're scoping Redwood for a proof-of-concept and potential annual commit: can you summarize the billing options for the hosted API? Specifically:

- Can we run on card for the POC and switch to monthly invoicing once we commit?
- Do you support Net30 / Net45 / Net60?
- How do you apply committed discounts or credits (e.g., if we prepay or commit to $200k+ ARR)?
- Any standard invoicing cadence (monthly in arrears vs monthly in advance) and how proration works if we change tier mid-quarter?

Procurement also asked for an example invoice and the current rate card so they can start the internal approvals.

Thanks — Drew
Drew Collins
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
procurement@acme-analytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Drew Collins <drew@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence and invoicing for hosted API

Hi Drew — thanks for the clear list. Long answer short: yes to card for a POC, and yes we can switch to invoicing on a regular cadence once you move to a committed plan. Details below and I attached the rate card + a sample invoice template for procurement.

Payment methods and cadence:
- Card (auto-bill): immediate activation, pay-as-you-go. Good for POCs and low-friction onboarding.
- Monthly invoice (default for accounts with volume or PO requirements): invoices issued monthly in arrears; standard is Net30. We can support Net45 for enterprise contracts and exceptions on a case-by-case basis. Net60 is uncommon and requires finance approval and credit checks.
- For annual committed agreements we offer an invoice option (monthly invoices with committed discount applied) or an upfront prepay/credit purchase. Upfront credits are issued as account balance and consumed first.

Discounts and committed pricing:
- Standard committed discount bands (examples): 5% for annual committed spend > $50k, 12% for > $200k.
- For larger strategic commitments (> $250k/year) we typically negotiate deeper discounts (finance approval required).
- Discounts apply to billable units post-commit; if you prepay, credits are applied pro-rata to consumption.

Proration and mid-period changes:
- If you increase committed tier mid-quarter, we prorate forward: you pay the difference for the remaining period; consumption is billed against the committed amount first.
- For downgrades mid-term, we do not credit retroactively for prior usage; changes take effect next billing period unless otherwise negotiated.

Invoicing mechanics and procurement needs:
- We accept PO numbers and can add them to the invoice.
- Payment methods for invoices: ACH (preferred), wire, and card on file (for convenience).
- Tax/VAT: invoices will include tax where applicable; we can accept your resale certificate if needed.

Attachments I included: rate_card_Q1_2026.pdf, sample_invoice_template.pdf.

If you can share a target committed spend or expected run-rate for Year 1, I can model 2–3 scenarios (monthly invoice with Net30, monthly invoice Net45, upfront credits with prepay) and show the effective unit economics. If procurement wants a PO-to-invoice flow or a DocuSign SOW, let me know and I can loop in our contracts team.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Drew Collins <drew@acme-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence and invoicing for hosted API

Ben — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

1) Our target first-year committed spend is ~$350k (proof-of-value in Q2, go-live in Q3). Would you be able to confirm the discount band for that level and whether we could get the discounted rates applied immediately if we sign a DocuSign SOW?

2) We prefer Net45 but procurement has pushed for Net60 for some vendors. If Net60 is possible, what additional documentation or credit checks are required?

3) If we opt for upfront credits (prepay) to get slightly better economics, how do you handle expirations and refunds if our usage is lower than estimated?

Can you also confirm who will be the point of contact for the invoice/PO processing (AP team) so I can share it with our finance team?

Thanks — Drew

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Drew Collins <drew@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-26T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence and invoicing for hosted API

Drew — answering inline and looping in Laura (manager) and Priyom from finance for the Net60 / prepay specifics. Quoting your points below.

> 1) Our target first-year committed spend is ~$350k. Would you confirm the discount band and application?

For $350k/year we can offer a negotiated discount. Standard published band is 12% for $200k+, but I asked Laura for discretionary authority. We can provisionally apply up to 18% off the hosted API list rates for an initial 12-month SOW, subject to finance sign-off and a signed DocuSign. We'll formalize in the SOW — Laura, can you confirm?

> 2) Net45 vs Net60

Net45 is straightforward and commonly approved for enterprise contracts. Net60 requires a finance review and a credit check; Priyom, can you advise what information Acme would need to provide for a Net60 evaluation? (Typical items: bank references, recent financials, or an agreed prepayment schedule.)

> 3) Upfront credits expiration/refund policy

If you prepay: credits are valid for 12 months from purchase by default. Refunds are possible for unused credits on a case-by-case basis; finance will evaluate. For large prepayments we can offer a custom refund window in the contract.

AP contact: Priyom Das (priyom_das@redwood.com) handles billing operations and invoice routing. I'll include a sample AP routing block in the SOW.

I'll prepare a brief pricing model (three rows: monthly invoice Net45; monthly invoice Net30; upfront prepay with 18% discount) and return it with the SOW and DocuSign link.

Best,
Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence and invoicing for hosted API

Ben / Priyom — I reviewed. Approve the following guardrails:

- Authorize a standard committed discount of 15% for annual commitments between $200k–$300k.
- For commitments >= $300k, Ben may provisionally offer up to 18% pending final finance sign-off. Any offer above 18% needs director-level approval.
- Net45 is acceptable; Net60 requires a basic credit review (bank reference + 12 months of financials) and explicit sign-off from finance lead.
- Prepay credit expiration: 12 months by default. Refunds require finance approval; offer a limited refund window for strategic customers only.

Priyom — please draft the DocuSign SOW template with an AP contact block and include the sample_invoice_template.pdf as the invoice appendix. Once drafted, Ben can send to Acme.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Drew Collins <drew@acme-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>

Ben / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and clarity.

Acme is comfortable moving forward with the following provisional terms: 12-month SOW, target committed spend $350k, apply 18% discount contingent on finance sign-off and standard credit check. We prefer Net45; Net60 is a non-starter for us.

Next steps for us: please send DocuSign SOW and a preliminary invoice/PO instructions so we can route internally. Procurement will begin the credit documentation if required.

Thanks — Drew
